entities.how_described: 本集说 Elastic 的 semantic text 默认按句子边界切成 250 token 块，可配置到词、段落、页面粒度

evidence.quote: We've heard of chunking.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: We do help with chunking.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And so you can configure chunking down to the word, to paragraph, page boundary, things like that.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: There are frameworks that talk about semantic chunking and there are other labels for what I will call
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: Large context window chunking.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: We actually, and this is talked about in the lab in the later sections, we do have a technique that we use called late chunking that can work on large context windows.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: That's the closest thing that I would say we would have to semantic chunking.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: But we don't really have a need for that construct because the semantic text field itself allows us to deliver the same thing you would get with semantic chunking just by chunking the data and then running searches across it.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: So we would solve the problem with traditional chunking and hybrid search, not any exotic semantic chunking scheme.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: chunking to real-time search, where the query gets translated into a query vector, and we do all the work for you under the hood.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: They are configurable, the chunking settings.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: They're not described in detail in the workshop, but if you go to the Elastic docs, you'll see what the configuration settings are for chunking.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

entities.name: HNSW
entities.how_described: 本集说 Elasticsearch 默认用 HNSW 分层可导航小世界图做近似最近邻检索，配合 int8/BBQ 量化降低内存开销

evidence.quote: HNSW, ANN.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: We do have other disk, we have disk, ANN, but by default we're using HNSW, the Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds Graph.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: So when it comes to work that we've done to make HNSW more efficient, that started two years ago, actually two plus years ago,
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: The only difference I would say between disk BBQ and BBQ is that we actually have an option in Elastic to not use HNSW as the underlying mechanism for search.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And it just does HNSW or one of the disk algorithms and returns a set of documents.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: ESQL
entities.how_described: 本集说 ESQL 是 Elastic 内新的类 SQL 管道式查询语言，参数化接入 MCP 工具调用链，是智能体搜索用例的最佳路径

evidence.quote: Who here knows or has heard of ESQL within Elastic?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: ESQL is a newer
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: So you can have ESQL tools to query documents in Elasticsearch.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And the last thing I'll say about, I'm a big fan of ESQL.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: I started out a little bit skeptical because there were some features in Elastic Query Language that weren't in ESQL.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: I think that it's feature complete enough for you to at least take a look at it, especially if you're building agentic search use cases, because there's some really cool concepts in ESQL
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: that lend themselves well to solving for certain search tasks better than Elastic Query Language, which you should consider a superset of what ESQL is today.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And the other thing about ESQL that makes it fantastic is the ability to have parametrization wired into the MCP tool calling chain and wired up with Agent Builder, which is a fantastic add that technically is doable outside of ESQL,
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: The way that we have architected ESQL and our agent builder and our MCP endpoint, it is the happy path to a lot of the, let's call them agentic search use cases that you might have.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: So if you have not looked at ESQL yet, highly recommend you do that.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: First place to look is actually going through the ESQL docs and seeing what new novel retrieval mechanisms we're coming up with because we're doing some very interesting things with federated searching, potentially calling out the different systems within an elastic query language, you know, query that is not considered traditional elastic.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And when it does, ESQL is going to be your gateway into that.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And I'm talking about things like being able to do like parquet queries on things that are external to Elastic with an ESQL call, which could be incredibly powerful if you're also joining that with data that comes from Elastic.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: You can actually see that the agent used ESQL for this call.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And I'd say that that was the primary reason we started building ESQL was to build the best in class search experience so people could get rid of all their Splunk stuff.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: It's changed a little bit over the years if you haven't used it in a little while, but now you can do ESQL in there.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01
